# MACROBUTTON labels

Original OPC/XML fixture generated by `tools/macro_button_fixture.py`. It contains
no macro project or executable code. The reference application exported the reference on
2026-09-18 without saving changes to the source. Hashes and extracted text are
recorded in `reference.json`.

The nine rows cover unquoted and quoted labels, instructions split across runs,
stale cached results, locked fields, simple fields, adjacent buttons, a quoted
command name and a non-MACROBUTTON field. The split label is bold blue followed
by italic red. The reference application displays the instruction label even for locked/stale caches.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.16.5.34 defines the result as field-argument-2. The general
field-argument grammar (§17.16.1) permits surrounding quote delimiters. The reference application
instead displays those quotes literally for this field, including the trailing
space in the quoted-label row. The preview reproduces this measured compatibility
behavior. The command name is neither displayed nor executed.

The reference application refreshed the control DATE field to 9/18/2026. Our preview intentionally
retains its saved `Cached date` result; this change does not implement general
field evaluation. Both applications render the fixture on one page. Browser
tests verify label formatting, read-only typing and byte-identical download;
unit tests additionally cover malformed/nested fields and XML immutability.

## Native editing evidence

`python tools/macro_button_fixture.py --editing` creates `editing.docx`, the
same original controls with the unrelated DATE row omitted. It is the independent
control for editable body prompts.
`tools/record_macro_button_edits.ps1` records ten selection operations in a
private reference application instance with macros disabled. `native-edits.json` binds the native
body XML, field inventory and selection ranges to the source SHA-256.

Selecting a visible field and typing `Author` removes the complete field,
including stale cached content. This also holds for locked, simple, quoted and
split-format controls. Shift+Right from the prompt's start selects the entire
prompt; Right crosses it and subsequent typing inserts ordinary text outside
the field. Applying italic to the selected prompt instead preserves its code
and sets the instruction run's formatting. A direct hidden-code range probe
appends to the instruction rather than replacing the visible label; it must
not be used as evidence for ordinary prompt replacement. The recorded
`before.end` is COM `Result.End`, not always the whole field's end: selected
cached fields include one additional closing delimiter.

`tests/macro-button-native-edits.test.js` checks the source hash, native field
removal/preservation, boundary behavior, and projection of the resulting XML.
These are native compatibility evidence tests, supplemented by the model and
browser editing tests below. No macros were run or added.

The instruction-label codec is covered by `tests/macro-button-codec.test.js`:
untouched envelope retention, native italic display, split label formatting,
cache/lock/dirty preservation, simple-to-complex conversion, and rejection of
text replacement or metadata that conversion would discard. A generated copy
with all nine prompts italicized was schema-validated and opened in the
reference application: it renders on one page, retains all labels, and displays the italic
labels including the converted simple field. The split control retains its blue
bold and red formatting. Scratch evidence is `<work>/macro-codec-italic.docx`,
`macro-codec-italic-word.pdf` and `macro-codec-italic-word.png` in the task workspace.
The codec is now integrated into body import/export. `macro-button-editing.test.js`
covers native replacement cases, formatting, boundary insertion/deletion, search,
bookmarks/hyperlinks, unrelated-part preservation, reopen, and exact undo. The
browser workflow checks atomic keyboard/native selections, replacement, formatting
a simple field, deletion, exported packages and editable reopening. The original
fixture containing DATE remains read-only because that unrelated field is not
supported for editing.
